snippets.output: Meningitis is an inflammation of the protective membranes covering the brain and spinal cord, known as the meninges.
snippets.pattern_notes: Definition + naming of the membranes: enumeration of properties of meningitis.

snippets.output: Meningitis can be caused by various infectious agents, including bacteria, viruses, fungi, and parasites, as well as non-infectious causes such as certain medications and autoimmune diseases.
snippets.pattern_notes: Enumerates infectious and non-infectious causes of meningitis.

snippets.output: Symptoms of meningitis can include sudden onset of fever, headache, stiff neck, nausea, vomiting, increased sensitivity to light (photophobia), and altered mental status.
Diagnosis of meningitis typically involves clinical evaluation, lumbar puncture to analyze cerebrospinal fluid (CSF), and laboratory tests to identify the causative agent.
snippets.pattern_notes: Enumeration of diagnostic steps for meningitis.

snippets.output: Treatment of meningitis depends on the underlying cause. Bacterial meningitis requires prompt antibiotic therapy, while viral meningitis may only require supportive care.
snippets.pattern_notes: Lists treatment approaches by cause type.

snippets.output: Vaccination is available for some types of bacterial meningitis and is an effective preventive measure.
snippets.pattern_notes: Parallel properties of vaccination: availability and effectiveness.

snippets.output: Bacterial meningitis is often more severe and can lead to serious complications or death if not treated promptly.
snippets.pattern_notes: Severity claim extended by consequence if untreated; causal chain.

snippets.output: Common bacterial pathogens causing meningitis include Streptococcus pneumoniae, Neisseria meningitidis, and Haemophilus influenzae type b (Hib).
Viral meningitis is generally less severe and often resolves without specific treatment.
snippets.pattern_notes: Parallel properties of viral meningitis: severity and resolution.

snippets.output: Common viral causes of meningitis include enteroviruses, herpes simplex virus, and varicella-zoster virus.
